faqs.a: Luminosity weights channels by how bright humans perceive them (green 71%, red 21%, blue 7%) — the most realistic grey. Average treats all channels equally. Lightness (HSL) averages the brightest and darkest channels. For photos and UI, luminosity is the standard choice.
faqs.q: Which greyscale method should I use?

faqs.a: No — it removes chroma only. The result is a neutral grey with the same perceived brightness as the original. Hue information is gone, so the conversion cannot be reversed.
faqs.q: Is greyscaling the same as darkening?

faqs.a: Yes — type any 3- or 6-digit HEX code in the text box, or use the color picker swatch. Invalid input is ignored so the result never breaks.
faqs.q: Can I type a HEX code directly?

faqs.a: No — the conversion math runs locally in JavaScript. Nothing leaves your device.

color-desaturator.formula:
luminosity: grey = 0.2126 x R + 0.7152 x G + 0.0722 x B
average: grey = (R + G + B) / 3
lightness: grey = (max(R,G,B) + min(R,G,B)) / 2
result = rgb(grey, grey, grey)

color-desaturator.workedExample:
Take #4f46e5 = rgb(79, 70, 229).
Luminosity: 0.2126 x 79 = 16.795; 0.7152 x 70 = 50.064; 0.0722 x 229 = 16.534; sum = 83.39, rounds to 83 -> rgb(83, 83, 83) = #535353.
Average: (79 + 70 + 229) / 3 = 378 / 3 = 126 -> #7e7e7e.
Lightness: (229 + 70) / 2 = 149.5, rounds to 150 -> #969696.
Same color, three defensible greys — luminosity (#535353) best matches how bright the color looks.
